messages.content: You write dialogue that reveals character through voice and rhythm.
Write a dialogue between a detective and a suspect during interrogation. The detective bluffs about having evidence. The suspect is innocent but acts guilty out of fear.

message.content:
# THE INTERVIEW

---

The room smelled of cold coffee and older regrets. DETECTIVE MARLA VANCE (52) sat across from DANIEL HAYES (34), a man whose hands hadn't stopped moving since they sat down—now gripping his own knees, now finding each other, now reaching for the water glass and abandoning it halfway.

Vance studied him. The sweat at his temples. The way his eyes kept sliding to the door.

"We found the knife," she said.

It was a lie. They had no knife. They had a witness who placed him near the scene and nothing else. But Vance had been doing this long enough to know that "nothing else" was sometimes enough.

Daniel's face went pale. "Wh—what knife?"

"The one you used." Vance leaned back. Casual. Almost bored. "The one with your prints all over it."

"I wasn't—there." He stopped. Swallowed. "I wasn't there. I wasn't anywhere near—"

"Daniel." She said his name like a parent tired of a child's excuses. "We have you on camera three blocks from the scene at 11:47. The victim died at 11:52. That's a five-minute window. You want to explain that?"

His mouth opened. Closed. Opened again.

"I was walking. I was just walking. I go walking at night when I can't sleep, and I—"

"Three blocks from a murder scene. At night. Walking."

"I know how it looks."

"How do you think it looks, Daniel?"

He looked at the table. At his hands. At anything but her.

---

Vance had seen guilty men. She knew the way they held themselves—the false calm, the rehearsed confusion, the way they'd already built their alibi in their head and were just waiting to deliver it. Daniel wasn't like that. Daniel was a mess of raw, unfiltered panic.

But she'd also learned that innocent people didn't usually end up in interrogation rooms.

"You were seen going into the building," Vance continued. "The one next door. The one with the fire escape that leads directly to the roof of the victim's residence."

"I went in to use the bathroom. I swear to God, I went in to use the bathroom, there was nobody around, I didn't see anyone, I didn't hear anything, I just—"

"The building was locked."

"I picked the lock." His voice cracked on the admission. "I know how that sounds. I know. But I really just needed to use the bathroom, and the door was—"

"You picked a lock. To use a bathroom."

"I'm sorry. I'm sorry, I shouldn't have, but I was desperate, and I—"
